What this scan could not evidence

The highest level this run could have stated for any agent is H1 Registered. A criterion nobody answered counts as not met, so no agent is shown above that level, whatever its real state.

The bar is H2 for an agent that only reads and H3 for one that can write or reach outside the estate. This run could not have shown any agent at its bar, so every judged agent is reported below it. That is a limit of what was read, stated here so it is not mistaken for a failure a source observed.

Agents and criteria

An agent reaches a level only when every criterion on it and below it is evidenced. A level is stated only for an agent every relevant source was read in full for.

  • E Evidenced: a source observed it
  • D Evidenced on what the operator declared in the inventory, not observed
  • M Reported met without evidence; counts as not met
  • N Not met: a source saw it fail
  • n Not met on what the operator declared in the inventory; no source saw it fail
  • · Unanswered: a configured reader could have reported it and none did; counts as not met
  • – Not readable: nothing this run was configured to read could have reported it; counts as not met

Unregistered identities

An unregistered automated identity is a principal that no register or inventory names, and that shows no sign of a model: it was not in agent code, in a tracing system or on an MCP server, and its report lists no tool and no model endpoint. A build workflow that holds a key, or a service account, looks like this.

The scan cannot show that one of these runs no model. Each is a finding of medium severity, and none is held to the agent bar. If one is an agent, register it or add it to the inventory, and it is then scored as one. If it is not, it still needs an owner on record.
